questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) is located in which town in Osun State?
questions.explanation: OAU is located in Ile-Ife, a historic town in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What was Obafemi Awolowo University originally named when it was founded in 1962?
questions.explanation: The institution was established in 1962 as the University of Ife before being renamed in 1987.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year was the University of Ife officially renamed Obafemi Awolowo University?
questions.explanation: The university was renamed Obafemi Awolowo University in 1987 in honour of Chief Obafemi Awolowo, a prominent Nigerian statesman.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: After whom is Obafemi Awolowo University named?
questions.explanation: The university is named after Chief Obafemi Awolowo, a Nigerian nationalist and the first Premier of the Western Region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Ile-Ife, home to OAU, is traditionally regarded by the Yoruba people as what?
options: The capital of the old Northern Region
The site of the first Nigerian parliament
The location of Nigeria's first seaport
questions.explanation: Ile-Ife holds deep cultural and historical significance as the traditional cradle of Yoruba civilization, according to Yoruba oral history and tradition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which traditional ruler is the recognised paramount monarch based in Ile-Ife?
questions.explanation: The Ooni of Ife is the traditional monarch of Ile-Ife and one of the most revered traditional rulers among the Yoruba people.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: OAU's main campus is widely noted for which distinctive architectural feature?
options: A campus built solely of mud brick huts
questions.explanation: OAU is well known for its distinctive modernist campus architecture, designed in the 1960s and often cited as a landmark of Nigerian architectural design.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which UNESCO World Heritage Site, associated with Yoruba religion and culture, is located in Osun State?
questions.explanation: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, located along the banks of the Osun River in Osogbo, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which river is closely associated with the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove and its annual festival?
questions.explanation: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove sits along the Osun River, and the annual Osun-Osogbo Festival celebrates the river goddess Osun.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the capital city of Osun State?
questions.explanation: Osogbo is the capital of Osun State, while Ile-Ife remains historically and culturally significant as the seat of the Ooni.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Osun State was carved out of which larger state in 1991?
questions.explanation: Osun State was created in August 1991 out of the former Oyo State during Nigeria's state creation exercise under General Ibrahim Babangida.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which ethnic group forms the predominant population of Osun State and Ile-Ife?
questions.explanation: Osun State, including Ile-Ife, is predominantly inhabited by the Yoruba ethnic group.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which regulatory body is responsible for accrediting academic programmes in Nigerian universities, including OAU?
options: The Federal Ministry of Education alone, with no separate agency
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB)
questions.explanation: The NUC is the regulatory body responsible for approving and accrediting academic programmes offered by Nigerian universities, ensuring they meet minimum quality standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of a Vice-Chancellor in a Nigerian university, such as OAU?
options: Serving as the chief executive and academic head of the university
Serving as the elected student union president
Serving as an external auditor of the university's accounts
Managing only the university's sports facilities
questions.explanation: A Vice-Chancellor is the chief executive and principal academic officer of a Nigerian university, responsible for its overall administration and academic direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which arm of government in Nigeria is primarily responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary is the arm of government responsible for interpreting laws and adjudicating disputes, distinct from the law-making Legislature and law-enforcing Executive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following countries shares a land border with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares land borders with Niger, Chad, Cameroon, and Benin Republic; Ghana, South Africa, and Kenya are not bordering countries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert, spanning much of North Africa, is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)?
options: Organising and supervising elections in Nigeria
questions.explanation: INEC is Nigeria's independent body responsible for organising, conducting, and supervising elections at the federal and state levels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which cash crop has historically been a major export associated with Yoruba land, including areas around Osun State?
questions.explanation: Cocoa has historically been one of the most significant cash crops cultivated in south-western Nigeria, including areas around Osun State.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen's chemical symbol is simply 'O' on the periodic table.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars is known as the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface, giving it a reddish appearance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is Nigeria's national football team commonly nicknamed?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's senior men's national football team is popularly known as the Super Eagles, distinct from Ghana's Black Stars and Cameroon's Indomitable Lions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international body is primarily responsible for setting global standards and rules for international trade?
questions.explanation: The WTO is the international organisation specifically responsible for establishing and enforcing global rules governing trade between nations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a system of government headed by a king or queen whose powers are limited by a constitution?
questions.explanation: A constitutional monarchy is a system in which a monarch serves as head of state, but their powers are limited and defined by a constitution, unlike an absolute monarchy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a non-communicable disease, unlike tuberculosis, malaria, and cholera, which are infectious (communicable) diseases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, spanning parts of both Europe and Asia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is generally credited with leading the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, later founding the Sokoto Caliphate?
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio led the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, a religious and political reform movement that resulted in the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of the legislative arm of government?
questions.explanation: The legislative arm, such as Nigeria's National Assembly, is primarily responsible for making laws, distinct from the executive that enforces them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency is most commonly associated with the disease rickets?
questions.explanation: Rickets is a disease affecting bone development in children, most commonly caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period?
questions.explanation: GDP specifically measures the value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, regardless of the nationality of the producers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian playwright and author was the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, becoming the first African laureate in that category.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does the abbreviation 'NAFDAC' stand for in the Nigerian context?
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
National Authority for Food, Drugs, and Cosmetics
Nigerian Agency for Food and Drug Coordination
National Association for Drug and Chemical Control
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates and controls the manufacture, importation, and sale of food, drugs, and related products in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a persistent, sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy?
questions.explanation: Inflation describes an ongoing, generalised increase in prices across an economy, reducing the purchasing power of money.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)?
options: Restricting all trade between African nations
Creating a single market for goods and services across African countries to boost intra-African trade
questions.explanation: AfCFTA aims to create a single continental market for goods and services, boosting intra-African trade by reducing tariffs and other trade barriers among member states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a key function of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) relating to currency?
options: Setting the retail price of consumer goods
Issuing and regulating the country's currency (the Naira)
questions.explanation: One of the CBN's core functions is the sole authority to issue and regulate Nigeria's legal tender currency, the Naira.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
options: Coordinating international public health efforts and setting health standards
questions.explanation: WHO is a specialised United Nations agency focused on international public health, coordinating responses to health emergencies and setting global health standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is the largest producer of crude oil in Africa, based on long-established historical ranking?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has long been recognised as one of Africa's leading crude oil producers, historically ranking as the continent's largest producer for extended periods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the practice of a country restricting imports through tariffs or quotas to protect domestic industries?
questions.explanation: Protectionism refers to government policies that restrict international trade, such as tariffs and quotas, to shield domestic industries from foreign competition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Yoruba deity (Orisa) is traditionally associated with the Osun River and the Osun-Osogbo festival?
questions.explanation: The river goddess Osun is the deity traditionally celebrated at the annual Osun-Osogbo festival held at the sacred grove.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the legal document that formally establishes the rules and structure of governance for a country?
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental legal document that establishes the framework, powers, and limits of a country's system of governance.
